1. Heard Mr. Rajesh Mahale, learned Senior counsel
for  the  petitioner(s)  and  Mr.  Omar  Hoda,  Addl.
Advocate General for Respondent No.1.
2. The  present  Special  Leave  Petition  calls  in
1

--- Page 315 ---
question  the  correctness  of  the  judgment  dated
02.02.2026 in Crl. R.P. No.100332/2025 passed by the
High Court of Karnataka, Bench at Dharwad.
3. The petitioners stood chargesheeted for offences
punishable under Sections 306, 323, 354, 504, 506
read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and
Sections  3(2)(v)  and  3(2)(va)  of  the  Scheduled
Castes  and  the  Scheduled  Tribes  (Prevention  of
Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015 (for short, ‘SC/ST
Act’),  upon  the  complaint  lodged  by  the  2 nd
respondent.
4. Considering the nature of order we propose to
pass, we make a brief summary of the facts which are
necessary.
5. The brief facts, as available from the complaint
lodged by the wife of the deceased on 22.07.2023
with Police Station- Dharwad Sub Urban, Karnataka
was that the husband of the complainant had borrowed
Rs.10,00,000/-  from  one  Anand  Rao  K.  Pastey
(originally  arrayed  as  A-1)  at  the  rate  of  3%
monthly interest.
6. According to the complainant, for repayment of
loan, since there was default pursuant to COVID-19,
the husband of the complainant was made to execute a
registered sale deed in favour of the 1 st petitioner
herein,  Kareppa  @  Kariyappa.  According  to  the
complainant, even the amount of registration fee was
2

--- Page 316 ---
paid by her husband. It was further alleged that on
29.11.2019, the 1 st petitioner along with his family
visited the house of the complainant and threatened
them to vacate the house. Similar incidents were
alleged to have happened on 19.06.2023, 20.06.2023
and 15.07.2023.
7. According to the complainant, because of this
harassment, her husband committed suicide. It was on
her  complaint  that  an  FIR  was  registered  and
subsequently, charge-sheet was filed on 09.09.2023.
8. During the investigation, statements came to be
recorded and according to the prosecution, from the
statements  certain  other  offences  were  attracted
including the offences under the SC/ST Act.
9. It is not disputed that on 28.02.2025, the High
Court allowed the petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
of  Anand  Rao  K.  Pastey  (A-1),  and  quashed  the
proceedings  holding  that  the  ingredients  under
Section  306  of  the  IPC  were  not  attracted  and
further noticing that the disputes arose in the year
2019 and ultimately, incident happened in the year
2023 and the High Court found no proximity.
10. The petitioners herein moved an application for
discharge under Section 227 of Cr.P.C. before the II
Addl.  District  &  Sessions  Judge,  Dharwad.  That
petition was dismissed on 28.04.2025. Challenging
the same, the petitioners filed Criminal Revision
3

--- Page 317 ---
under Section 397 read with Section 401 of the
Cr.P.C., which has resulted in the impugned order.
11. The High Court has primarily held that the order
dated 28.04.2025 of the II Addl. District & Sessions
Judge, Dharwad was an order appealable under Section
14A of the SC/ST Act. In paragraph No.3, the High
Court held and recorded that the revision petition
was not maintainable. In spite of holding so, the
High Court in the next 03 paragraphs recorded that
prima  facie materials were available for proceeding
with the trial and upheld the order of discharge.
12. Both Mr. Rajesh Mahale, learned Senior counsel
and Mr. Omar Hoda, learned Addl. Advocate General
are ad idem  that an appeal indeed would lie against
the order dated 28.04.2025, under Section 14A of the
SC/ST Act.
13. Mr. Rajesh Mahale, learned Senior counsel, apart
from  the  above,  has  stated  that  having  found
revision under Section 397 and 401 of the Cr.P.C.
was not maintainable, the High Court could not have
entered into merits.
14. We are of the opinion that having found that the
revision was not maintainable, the High Court should
have stopped short and not gone based on merits.
15. For  the  reasons  stated  above,  we  set  aside
paragraph No(s).14, 15 and 16 of the impugned order
dated 02.02.2026 passed by the High Court.
4

--- Page 318 ---
16. We permit the petitioners to avail the remedy of
appeal  under  Section  14A  of  the  SC/ST  Act  to
challenge the order dated 28.04.2025 passed by the
II Addl. District & Sessions Judge, Dharwad.
17. If such an appeal is filed within four weeks from
today, the appeal shall not be dismissed on the
ground of limitation. We also direct that the appeal
will be heard independently on its own, uninfluenced
by any of the observations made by the High Court or
in the present order made by us.
18. When the matter came before us on 22.05.2026, we
had stayed the proceeding in Special SC & ST Case
No.54 of 2023 pending on the file of the II Addl.
District & Sessions Judge, Dharwad, Karnataka. We
direct that the order of stay will continue for a
period of 05 weeks from today.
19. With the above observations, the Special Leave
Petition  is  disposed  of  along  with  the  pending
application(s).

O R D E R
1. Appellant’s service was terminated by his employer. He claimed
reinstatement in service by instituting a suit 1 in the Court of the Civil
Judge, Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh. Upon the employer filing an
application under Order VII Rule 11, Code of Civil Procedure, 19082, the
plaint came to be rejected on the ground that Section 14(1)(b) of the
Specific Relief Act, 1963 was a bar to grant of such relief. The
impugned order of the High Court of Madhya Pradesh upheld such
order of rejection of plaint.
2. Having heard Mr. Romy Chacko, learned senior counsel for the
appellant/plaintiff and Mr. Balbir Singh, learned senior counsel for the
respondents/defendants, we are of the view that since a contract of
personal service cannot be specifically enforced, the relief of
reinstatement in service could not have been claimed by the appellant;
1 Civil Suit No.205-A/2016
2 CPC
1

--- Page 330 ---
to that extent, the trial court and the High Court are right. However,
had the appellant claimed the relief of damages, the suit would be
maintainable and the plaint not liable to rejection. Mr. Chacko submits
that since the application for rejection of plaint came to be allowed, he
did not have the opportunity to seek amendment of the plaint. 
3. Be that as it may, while setting aside the impugned orders of the
trial court and the High Court and reviving the appellant’s suit, we
dispose of the appeal granting liberty to the appellant to seek
amendment of the plaint by filing an application under Order VI Rule
17, CPC within four weeks from date.
4. If the proposed amendment is confined to amending the prayer
clause in the plaint by inserting the relief of damages, instead and in
place of reinstatement, with necessary averments in the body of the
plaint to support a right to claim such relief, the trial court may allow
the prayer for amendment.
5. As and when the application for amendment is allowed, the
defendant(s) shall be granted time to file written statement/additional
written statement.
6. Upon the pleadings being exchanged, the suit shall be taken to
its logical conclusion by the trial court in accordance with law.
7. If no application for amendment is filed by the appellant within
four weeks, this order shall stand recalled and the orders of the trial
court and the High Court restored.
2

--- Page 331 ---
8. The appeal is disposed of on the aforesaid terms, along with
connected interlocutory applications, if any, keeping all points and
contentions on merits open.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. We heard Ms. Madhavi Divan, the learned senior counsel
appearing for the petitioners and Mr. Mukul Rohatgi, the
learned senior counsel appearing for the respondent no.1.
2. We take notice of the what has been observed by the High
Court in para 64 of the impugned judgment. Para 64 reads
thus:-
“64. Since the matter stands remanded to the Appellate
Court for decision afresh and the order dated 08.07.2026
is set aside, hence, its effect would be that the order
of the Trial court would revive. Thus, in order to
protect  the  competing  interest  of  the  parties  and
noticing that the dispute also affects the functioning
of hospitals and a medical college run by the Public
Charitable Trust, accordingly, to protect and ensure
accountability of the parties without jeopardizing the
functioning of the Trust & its institutions, it is
provided that none of the bank accounts of the Trust
would be operated singly or jointly by the petitioner
and the respondent no.1 till the decision of the Appeal.
This Court directs that the said accounts of the Trust
and the two institutions shall be operated jointly, by
the petitioner and Sri Vikram Singh a founder trustee
and any amount withdrawn would be only for the basic
purposes of payment of salaries to the employees, staff
and Doctors of the Hospital and the Trust and any
recurring dues, if any, of banks and other financial
institutions, payment of public utility bills, statutory
dues, taxes or other like dues, and each withdrawal or
payment so made shall be placed before the Appellate
Court indicating the details, nature and purpose of the
payment so made. This arrangement will be operative till
the decision of the Appellate Court and thereafter it
2

--- Page 352 ---
would follow and abide with the order to be passed by
the Appellate Court.”
3. Thus, it appears that the High Court has remanded the
matter to the Appellate Court for de novo hearing and fresh
decision by set asiding the order dated 08 th July, 2026 passed
by the Appellate Court.
4. The trustees of the Charitable Trust are at war with each
other. This dispute is ultimately going to have a long lasting
effect on the administration of the Public Charitable Trust
which is running a medical college.
5. We are of the view that the trustees should sit together,
bury their differences in the larger interest of the Trust and
its beneficiaries.
6. Be that as it may, if the disputes are not resolved inter
se and ultimately the matter is to be heard on its own merits,
we direct that till a fresh decision is taken by the Appellate
Court, no major policy decisions shall be taken by the clients
of Mr. Mukul Rohatgi and all financial transactions during the
interregnum period shall be maintained in a separate account
statement.
7. In the peculiar facts of this case, we direct that the de
novo hearing be undertaken within a period of three weeks from
today and appropriate decision on its own merits shall be
taken by the Appellate Court, without being influenced by any
of the observations made by the High Court in its impugned
judgment.
3

--- Page 353 ---

disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.           OF 2026
(@ SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CRIMINAL) NO.12888/2026)
JINUSH      APPELLANT(S)
VERSUS
STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH     RESPONDENT(S)
ORDER
1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard learned counsel for the appellant and
learned counsel for the respondent-State of Uttar Pradesh.
3. This appeal is directed against the order dated
20.04.2026 passed by the High Court of Uttar Pradesh at
Allahabad  (briefly  the  ‘High  Court’  hereinafter),
rejecting the regular bail application of the appellant.
4. Appellant is an accused in FIR No.179/2024 registered
at Police Station- Mirzapur, District- Shahjahanpur, Uttar
Pradesh under Sections 323, 504, 506 and 307/34 of the
Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short, ‘IPC’).
5. The accusation against the appellant is that the
appellant was stalking the niece of the informant and when
the informant objected to the same, he stabbed him in the
stomach with a knife.
6. Appellant  was  arrested  on  18.05.2024  and  is  in
1

--- Page 367 ---
custody since then.
7. This Court had issued notice vide the order dated
24.07.2026, pursuant to which learned counsel for the
respondent-State  of  Uttar  Pradesh  has  filed  counter
affidavit.
8. Learned  counsel  for  the  appellant  submits  that
allegations against the appellant are general in nature.
Even in the FIR as well as in the evidence tendered by the
informant, nothing specific has been attributed to the
appellant. That apart, appellant is in custody for more
than 02 years now with the trial not likely to conclude
within a short period. In such circumstances, appellant
may be enlarged on bail.
9. Per contra , learned counsel for the respondent-State
of Uttar Pradesh submits that the allegation against the
appellant is specific and this has been borne out from the
evidence of the 02 prosecution witnesses, who have deposed
thus far. On a query by the Court, learned counsel for the
respondent-State of Uttar Pradesh submits that out of 07
witnesses, 02 witnesses have been examined. Next date
fixed by the Trial Court is on 29.09.2026. In such
circumstances, appellant may not be enlarged on bail.
10. Having regard to the submissions advanced at the Bar
and  the  period  of  incarceration  undergone  by  the
appellant, we are of the view that a case for bail is made
out. We are fortified in taking this view because the main
witnesses  have  already  been  examined.  The  remaining
2

--- Page 368 ---
witnesses are mostly official witnesses.
11. That being the position, t he impugned order dated
20.04.2026 passed by the High Court is set aside.
12. Consequently, we direct that the appellant shall be
produced before the jurisdictional Sessions Court within a
maximum period of 07 days from today, whereafter he shall
be released on bail on such terms and conditions as may be
deemed appropriate.
13. Accordingly, the Criminal Appeal is allowed.
14. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.
…………………………………………………...J.
      
   [UJJAL BHUYAN]
…………………………………………………...J.
     [ATUL S. CHANDURKAR]
NEW DELHI;
21st SEPTEMBER, 2026.

appellant’s bail application mainly on the
ground that on an earlier occasion, the
appellant was granted temporary bail to
perform  his  own  marriage,  which  never
happened.

after verifying the statement made in the

--- Page 371 ---
2

State stating that on verification, it is
found that appellant’s father is suffering
from IVth stage lung cancer.

appellant’s prayer for temporary bail so
that the appellant accompanies and lives
with his father for sometime.
6. Accordingly,  the  impugned  order
passed by the High Court is set aside and
it is directed that appellant be released

order, in connection with  First C.R. No.

on such terms and conditions as may be
imposed by the Trial Court. In addition,
appellant shall appear before the concerned

--- Page 383 ---
                   
                   
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Learned counsel for the petitioner, on 27.04.2026,
submitted before this Court that the petitioner was a
juvenile on the date of the  incident, i.e., 30.09.2012, as
he was aged about 16 years at the relevant time. It was
further submitted that the birth certificate issued by the
Municipal Board in the year 2020 recorded the petitioner's
date of birth as 15.07.1996. In view of the aforesaid claim
and the dispute regarding the petitioner's age, this Court
directed the District Judge to conduct an inquiry into the
actual date of birth of the petitioner.
2. Pursuant to the aforesaid direction, a detailed and
exhaustive inquiry was conducted. The inquiry report dated
03.07.2026,  submitted  by  the  learned  District  Judge,
reveals that the correct date of birth of the petitioner,
Somesh, is 15.07.1994. Consequently, on the date of the
incident, i.e., 30.09.2012, the petitioner was aged 18
years, 02 months and 15 days and, therefore, was a major on
the date of commission of the alleged offence.
3. The  inquiry  report  further  reveals  that  there
appears to have been a calculated attempt on the part of
the petitioner to obtain a birth certificate showing him to
be a minor on the date of the incident. The learned
2

--- Page 384 ---
District Judge has also noted lapses on the part of the
concerned authorities and has recorded findings regarding
the  manner  and  method  in  which  the  aforesaid  birth
certificate was obtained.
4. Taking note of the lapses and the manner in which
fraudulently a birth certificate was obtained, this Court
directs the Superintendent of Police, Ratlam, to register
an FIR and initiate appropriate criminal proceedings in
accordance with law against all the persons involved in the
matter. 
5. Let the necessary action be taken positively within
a period of 30 days from today.
6. The Superintendent of Police, Ratlam, shall submit a
compliance report before this Court upon completion of the
said period.
7. Registry is directed to communicate a copy of the
inquiry report of the District Judge, to the learned
counsel for the respondent-State of Madhya Pradesh and to
the Superintendent of Police, Ratlam, for necessary action
as ordered by this Court.
8. So far as the present Special Leave Petition on
merits  is  concerned,  keeping  in  view  the  concurrent
findings of fact recorded by the Trial Court and the High
Court, this Court does not find any reason to interfere
with  the  impugned  order  passed  by  the  High  Court.
Accordingly,  with  the  above  observation,  the  present
3

--- Page 385 ---
petition stands dismissed.
9. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

affirmed the conviction and sentence, which is the

murdered his younger brother, motivated by his

married a woman who had been previously married,
which  in  the  petitioner’s  eyes  had  allegedly
lowered  the  prestige  of  their  family.  It  is

found inside the same room at the same time, with

finding  of  guilt  and  the  resultant  sentence.
However,  considering  the  prolonged  period  of
incarceration of almost 24 years, we see that it
is a case fit for applying remission.  
4. The State has placed on record an Affidavit,
in which it is stated that the petitioner had
maintained good conduct in the Correctional Home
barring  an  instance  of  parole  jump,  and  had
received  favourable  recommendations  from  the

recommended  the  petitioner  for  remission,  the

any condition for surety by a third party, and

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL No.            /2026
[@ SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CRL.) NO. 14943/2026]
BRIJ KISHOR SINGH                     Appellant(s)
                      VERSUS
THE STATE OF BIHAR                   Respondent(s)
 O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
3. This appeal impugns order dated 08.07.2026
passed by the High Court of Judicature at Patna to
the extent it imposes a condition of deposit of
Rupees Four Lakhs for grant of anticipatory bail.
4. The submission on behalf of the appellant is
that according to the prosecution case, a tanker
carrying spurious diesel/petrol was seized.  The
appellant happens to be registered owner of the
tanker though he was not in possession of the
tanker at the time when the seizure was made.  The
case of the appellant is that the vehicle was
1

--- Page 403 ---
leased out and, therefore, he is not responsible
for carrying adulterated diesel/petrol.  Besides,
once the tanker has been seized, there was no
occasion for the High Court to impose condition of
deposit  of  Rupees  Four  Lakhs  for  grant  of
anticipatory bail.
5. We agree with the submission made on behalf
of the appellant that there was no justification
to impose condition of deposit of Rupees Four
Lakhs, particularly when the vehicle itself had
been seized.
6. Consequently, this appeal is allowed.  The
condition of deposit of Rupees four Lakhs as
imposed in the impugned order dated 08.07.2026 is
hereby quashed and set aside.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand
disposed of.

O R D E R
Pursuant to order dated 10.08.2026, Mr. Kamlesh Bahadur
(I.P.S.), presently posted as the Superintendent of Police,
Mau District, State of Uttar Pradesh, is present in the
Court and has filed an affidavit dated 29.08.2026.
2. On a query of the Court as to how many witnesses have
been examined since charges were framed against all six
1

--- Page 431 ---
(06) accused lastly on 27th March, 2023, the answer is that
02 out of 54 prosecution witnesses have been examined. We
are shocked at the conduct of the prosecution in not
ensuring that witnesses are produced before the Court for
more than three (03) years and, as of today, only two (02)
witnesses stand examined.
3. This leaves us in no doubt that the prosecution, which
is accountable for producing witnesses, has been absolutely
slack in its duty towards the Court in the conduct of
criminal trials. It is basically the investigating agency
which is under obligation to produce its witnesses, which
in the present case is the District Police.
4. The matter becomes more serious for the reason that, on
the one hand, the fourteen (14) year old son of the
petitioner was kidnapped on 27.09.2017 and till date, he
has neither been recovered nor his remains have been found,
whereas, on the other hand, despite submission of charge
sheet and even framing of charges in March, 2023 itself,
there is not even a semblance of seriousness shown by the
prosecuting agency in getting the trial concluded.
5. Accordingly, we direct the State of Uttar Pradesh to
initiate  departmental  proceedings  against  the
Superintendents of Police, Mau District, Uttar Pradesh, who
served from 2023 till date, for such casual approach
towards a duty cast upon them, especially in matters of
trial. The same shall be initiated within two (02) weeks
from today.
2

--- Page 432 ---
6. The Court would indicate that if it finds that the
charges served on the Superintendents of Police are only by
way of formality, the Court would take action against the
Competent Authority who issues the said memo of charges to
the Superintendents of Police, Mau District, Uttar Pradesh,
who held the post from the year 2023.
7. Post the matter on 16.11.2026 at 2:00 p.m.
8. An affidavit personally affirmed by the Chief Secretary
of the State of Uttar Pradesh bringing on record the action
taken shall be filed before the next date of listing.
9. The Registry shall communicate a copy of this order to
all concerned forthwith.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA

REVIEW PETITION (C) NO. 10542 OF 2026 
IN
SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (C) NO. 22530 OF 2026
SUBODH KUMAR SHAW        …      PETITIONER(S)
VERSUS
HOWRAH MUNICIPAL CORPORATION 
AND ORS.                  … RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. The present Review Petition has been preferred against the Order dated
03.07.2026 passed by this Court in SLP (C) No. 22530 of 2026, whereby the Special
Leave Petition filed against the judgment dated 11.06.2026 passed by the High Court
of Judicature at Calcutta (hereinafter referred to as “the High Court”) in MAT No. 949
of 2026 was dismissed.
2. We have perused the material placed on record. 
3. The challenge in the Special Leave Petition was essentially with regard to the
proposed demolition of two floors of the subject building. While dismissing the
Special Leave Petition, this Court had categorically observed that upon carrying out a
proper inspection, if it is found that any construction has been raised in violation of
the sanctioned building plan, the competent authorities shall take appropriate action in
1

--- Page 467 ---
accordance with law, including demolition of such unauthorised construction. The
Review Petition seeks reconsideration of the said order and, in substance, seeks
protection against the proposed demolition.
4. This Court has, in a catena of decisions, consistently held that unauthorised
constructions cannot be permitted to remain and that, where any construction is found
to be in violation of the sanctioned building plan or the applicable rules, the competent
authorities are required to take appropriate action, including demolition, after
following due process of law.
5. We find that no error apparent on the face of the record or any other ground
warranting review of the order dated 03.07.2026 has been made out.
6. Accordingly, the Review Petition is dismissed. 
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
……………………………………………………J.
    (R. MAHADEVAN)
……………………………………………………J.
    (ALOK ARADHE)

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA 
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION 
CIVIL APPEAL No.           OF 2026
[@ SLP (C) No. 25972 OF 2025]                           
KONSAM SUSHILA DEVI                                APPELLANT
                                VERSUS
NINGTHOUJAM GEOFFREY & ORS.                        RESPONDENTS
O R D E R
1.     Leave granted.
2.    This is a rather unusual case where we find that an Hon’ble Judge of the
High Court of Manipur at Imphal, sitting singly, has disposed of a contempt
petition1 alleging violation of an interim order on the ground that the original
proceeding2, in which such interim order was passed, is pending.
3. The  Contempt  of  Courts  Act,  1971  while  defining  ‘civil  contempt’  in
section 2(c) makes no distinction between a final order and an interim order. An
interim order, passed in aid of the final relief claimed in the proceedings, is after
all an order made by a court. If it were the law that an interim order need not
require compliance, that would result in total anarchy and chaos. The impugned
order passed by the Hon’ble Judge does not consider this aspect of the matter.
4. The  Hon’ble  Judge  has  also  failed  to  take  into  consideration  the
precedents3 set by this Court that even if a judicial order is passed, which could
be perceived as wrong by the party affected by it or bound thereby, that by
itself would not afford him ground to violate it unless a variation or quashing
thereof is obtained from the same court or superior court. So long that order
1  Contempt Case(C) No. 77 of 2025
2  WP(C) No. 279 of 2025
3  Nawabkhan Abbaskhan v. State of Gujarat : (1974) 2 SCC 121 (para.14), State of Punjab
v. Gurdev Singh : (1991) 4 SCC 1 (paras. 7 to 10) and Prithawi Nath Ram v. State of Jharkhand :
(2004) 7 SCC 261 (para.8)

--- Page 503 ---
2
subsists, the same would demand compliance failing which the violator would
expose himself to the consequences of contempt. 
5. We,  therefore,  see  no  reason  to  entertain  the  application  [I.A.
260823/2026] which has been filed by the respondents seeking dismissal of the
special leave petition; instead, we allow the appeal by setting aside the order
impugned.
6. Contempt Case (C) No. 77 of 2025 [arising out of W.P.(C) No. 279 of 2025]
shall stand revived on the file of the High Court. Let the same be taken to its
logical conclusion in accordance with law.
7. All contentions on merits are kept open to be urged by the parties before
the relevant court.
8. The  application  [I.A.  260823/2026]  seeking  directions,  consequently,
stands dismissed.
9. The appeal is allowed on the above terms.
10. Pending interlocutory application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
…………….............................J.
[DIPANKAR DATTA]
……………..............................J.
[SHEEL NAGU]
New Delhi;
September 21, 2026.

C.A. No.  7871 OF 2024          1 
 
 
 
 
 
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA 
       CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION 
 
 
CIVIL APPEAL NO(S).  7871 OF 2024 
(Arising out of SLP (C) No. 32995 OF 2018) 
 
 
  
HINDUSTAN CABLES LIMITED & ANR.      …APPELLANT(S) 
 
                                  VERSUS 
 
 K SRI RAMASHARMA & ORS.                 …RESPONDENT(S) 
 
 
 
O R D E R  
 
 
1. The present appeal challenges the order dated 
20.11.2018 passed by the High Court in a Writ Appeal 
whereby the benefit of revised pay scales have been granted 
to the respondent(s) with effect from 01.01.1997 to 
31.03.2001 on having opted for and allowed voluntary 
retirement. 
2. It may be noted here that respondent No(s). 1, 3, 12 
and 17 have since expired and no application for 
impleadment of their legal representatives has been filed by 

--- Page 518 ---
C.A. No.  7871 OF 2024          2 
the appellant(s). Vide order dated 13.01.2020, the Special 
Leave Petition qua them was ordered to be abated. In the 
absence of any application for impleadment of their legal 
representatives till date, the appeal(s) qua respondent(s) No. 
1, 3, 12 and 17 shall stand abated and the judgment under 
challenge in this appeal has attained finality for them.  
3. We have heard the learned counsel(s) appearing for the 
parties at length. It is an undisputed fact that similarly 
situated employees, who had sought voluntary retirement 
and were so permitted, were released pay revision benefits 
in terms of the decision of the appellant -Company, 
pursuant to the judgment passed by the High Court. 
4. The said judgment when challenged before this Court, 
came to be affirmed with the dismissal on 29.03.2016 of 
the Special Leave Petition preferred by the appellant(s). 
5. Learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant(s) 
has sought to distinguish the case of the respondent(s) 
herein viz a viz the employees who have been granted the 
benefit of the above referred lis but we are of the considered 
view that there is no such distinction which can be culled 
out in the particular facts and circumstances of this case. 

--- Page 519 ---
C.A. No.  7871 OF 2024          3 
6. We, therefore, dismiss the present appeal in the 
peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case. 
7. Pending applications(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

TRANSFER PETITION (CIVIL) NO. 2489 OF 2025
EKTA PETITIONER(S)
VERSUS
AASHU SHARMA RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. The petitioner-wife seeks transfer of Petition No.1283 of
2004,  titled  as  “Aashu  Sharma  v.  Smt.  Ekta” ,  filed  by  the
respondent-husband under Section 13(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act,
1955.  The above-stated case is pending before the learned Judge,
Family Court, No.1, Jodhpur, Metropolitan (Rajasthan) and the
petitioner prays for its transfer to the Family Court, Bijnor,
Uttar Pradesh.
2. It is submitted that the petitioner is unemployed, residing at
Bijnor with her minor daughter, and cannot undertake 900 km/12-13
hrs journey to Jodhpur.  Additionally, three proceedings against
the  respondent-husband  are  already  pending  at  Bijnor.   The
petitioner-wife also relies on alleged matrimonial cruelty and
dowry demands to seek the transfer.  
3. Keeping in view the nature of the proceedings, the instant
Transfer Petition is allowed.  Accordingly, Petition No.1283 of
2004, titled as “ Aashu  Sharma  v. Smt.  Ekta”, pending before the
learned  Judge,  Family  Court,  No.1,  Jodhpur,  Metropolitan
(Rajasthan) is ordered to be transferred to the Family Court,
Bijnor, Uttar Pradesh. The respondent-husband is permitted to
1

--- Page 551 ---
participate in the proceedings through video conferencing unless
otherwise directed by the Court.  The records shall be transferred
to the transferee court.

       (JOYMALYA BAGCHI)
..........................J.
       (V. MOHANA)

Exemption is granted from filing official translation. 
In the light of the law laid down in Shiv Pratap Singh Alias
Chinu  v.  State  of  U.P.  &  Ors. 1,  issue  notice,  returnable
05.11.2026.
1  2026 INSC 894
1

--- Page 573 ---
We find that a caveat has been field on behalf of the
complainant in one of the First Information Reports lodged against
the petitioner. Though the said complainant was not heard by the
High Court also, we deem it appropriate to permit him to come on
record as respondent No. 6. 
Complainant is impleaded as respondent No. 6. 
Cause title shall be amended accordingly. 
Mr.  Shwetank  Sailakwal,  who  is  present  in  Court  on
caveat/advance notice, waives service and accepts notice on behalf
of newly impleaded respondent No. 6/the complainant. Hence, notice
need not be serve on the said respondent. 
Notice to the unrepresented respondents shall be served by all
modes, including dasti. 
In the meanwhile, further proceedings against the petitioner

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following

1. The subject matter of challenge before us is an interlocutory
Order passed by the High Court in First Appeal preferred by the
respondent. 
2. The nature of the interlocutory order is stay of the execution
of the money decree unconditionally.
3. The matter before us is at the stage of notice.

--- Page 605 ---
2
4. It appears that in the meantime, the main matter, i.e. First
Appeal Number 2181 of 2018, came up for hearing before a Division
Bench of the High Court. The High Court has passed the following
order dated 14th September, 2026:-
“1. Having heard Ms. Megha Jani, learned Senior Counsel assisted
by Mr. Mit S. Thakkar, learned advocate for the appellant and
Mr. Apurva Vakil, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Mr. P.M.
Lakhani, learned advocate for the respondent and perused the
record, noticing that the dispute essentially is between two
brothers and one of them holds a money decree against another,
we are of the considered view that an attempt be made by the
parties to resolve their dispute amicably.
2. On this suggestions of the Court, the learned Senior counsels
appearing for the parties would submit that the parties are
ready and willing to participate in the mediation process.
3. In view of the above, the matter is referred to the MED-ARB
Centre  of  the  Gujarat  High  Court  Arbitration  Centre  where
advocates well versed in commercial matters are empanelled as
Mediators. We request the Gujarat High Court Arbitration Centre
to provide two Mediators who may act as co-mediator to engage
with the parties and make an effort to find out an amicable
solution.
4. Both the parties are hereby directed to deposit an amount of
Rs.25,000/- each to be paid to the Mediators as one time fees.
The notice of the date fixed for mediation shall be intimated to
the parties through their learned advocates appearing in this
matter. The matter be posted along with the mediation report.
5. Needless to say that the observations in this order about the
nature of dispute is only our understanding for the purpose of
referring the matter to mediation.”
 5. Thus, the parties have been referred for mediation. 
 6. In view of the aforesaid, we expect the parties to appear
before the Mediator, Mediation and Arbitration Center of the
Gujarat High Court, within a period of one week from today. 
7. We expect the parties to cooperate in the mediation. 
8. Post it after six weeks.

         UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. We have heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.
2. The petitioner challenges the order dated 19.11.2025 and prays
for grant of enhanced interim maintenance.
3. After perusing the record and noting the findings recorded in
the impugned order, we are of the view that the interim maintenance
awarded by the High Court at the rate of Rs. 1,00,000/- (Rupees One

--- Page 637 ---
2
Lakh only) per month be substituted with Rs. 1,25,000/- (Rupees One
Lakh Twenty-Five Thousand Only) per month.
4. The  learned  counsel  for  the  respondent  argues  that  the
respondent has been duly and properly complying with the orders
passed by the Court. Considering his present financial position,
the respondent has already moved the Trial Court to reduce the
maintenance determined by the order dated 31.07.2024 read with
19.11.2025.  It  is  further  stated  that  the  respondent  faces
financial difficulties and that the Court may not enhance the
interim maintenance.
5. We take note of the submission and, taking into account the
social standing of the parties and the findings of fact regarding
the respondent’s income, we enhance the sum from Rs. 1,00,000/-
(Rupees One Lakh only) to Rs. 1,25,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Twenty-
Five Thousand Only). The respondent continues to pay Rs. 1,25,000/-
(Rupees One Lakh Twenty-Five Thousand Only) per month. As for
arrears, the respondent is given liberty to pay in four equal
installments, with the first installment falling due on 15.12.2026.
6. The Special Leave Petition is disposed of with the above
modification.
7. The order in the Special Leave Petition is without prejudice
to the contentions available to both the parties.
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The petitioner who is aggrieved by the impugned order, by which High Court
refused to interfere with the order to transfer, is before this Court.
2.  Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, we are not
inclined to interfere with the impugned order since the principle of transfer,
being an incidence of the service, squarely applies to petitioner also.
1

--- Page 695 ---
3.  Be that as it may. It is the grievance of the petitioner that for the
qualification he possesses, there is no infrastructure available for teaching the
students or training the students in sports activities. If it is so, we grant liberty
to the petitioner to make appropriate representation before the jurisdictional
authorities for his posting and the authorities would be at liberty to consider the
said representation on its own merits and pass appropriate orders. 
4.  We make it explicitly clear that we have not directed that petitioner should
be granted any particular posting or otherwise and it is made clear that it is left
to the discretion of the authorities to pass appropriate orders taking into
consideration the grievances of the petitioner that may be vented out through
his representation. It is also made clear that there is no need or necessity of
affording any personal hearing.
5. With these observations, the Special Leave Petition stands dismissed.
6. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

“40. In cases under NDPS Act, the proof of
integrity  of  the  samples  is  absolutely

prove the safe custody of the samples, inasmuch
as the whereabouts of the samples from 9 th
1

--- Page 785 ---
October,  2018  to  30 th October,  2018  have
remained a mystery. The Malkhana Register has
not been produced to unravel this mystery. It
would be unsafe to rely upon the report of the
FSL in the facts and circumstances of the case
as it has not been established that the samples
which were examined by the FSL are the same
that were drawn from the substance recovered
from  the  search  of  house  of  the
appellant/accused.  The  prosecution,  in  the
instant case, has clearly failed to establish
the integrity of the samples.”
3. That apart, there is delay of 309 days in filing
the present Special Leave Petition.

the ground of delay as well as on merits.

disposed of.

For Respondent(s): Mr. Nikunj Arora, Adv.
                   Mr. Md. Noor Alam, Adv.
                   Mr. Parth Johri, Adv.
                   Mr. Ashish Pandey, AOR
                   Mr. Akhil Kumar, Adv.                   
                   
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. We have heard Mr. Anil Kaushik, learned Addl.
Solicitor General for the petitioner(s).
2. Delay condoned.
3. Learned Addl. Solicitor General relies on the
Office Memorandum dated 02.11.2012 as well as the
Office Memorandum dated 14.09.1992 to assail the
1

--- Page 793 ---
direction of the High Court for opening the sealed
cover of the respondent.
4. However, the office memorandum dated 02.11.2012
referring to the decision of this Court in Union of
India versus K.V. Jankiraman [AIR 1991 SC 2010]  has
clarified  that  when  it  is  a  matter  of
corruption/dereliction of duty etc. and there is a
serious  complaint  with  matter  still  under
investigation, the Government would be within its
right to place such official under suspension, in
which event his case for promotion would be placed
under sealed cover.
5. Insofar  the  present  case  is  concerned,  the
related  FIR  against  the  respondent  has  been
registered under Sections 498A and 406/34 of the
Indian Penal Code, 1860.
6. In  such  circumstances,  the  aforesaid  Office
Memorandum would have no application to the facts of
this case.
7. We find no merit in the challenge to the impugned
judgment and order of the High Court.
8. Accordingly,  the  Special  Leave  Petition  is
dismissed.
9. Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  stand
disposed of.
(ABHINAV KUMAR)                                (CHETNA BALOONI)

                             O R D E R
Issue notice to the respondents.
Learned counsel for the first respondent-Caveator
accepts notice.
Notice to the second respondent is dispensed with.
We  have  heard  learned  senior  counsel  for  the
petitioner as well as learned senior counsel for the first
respondent  –  Caveator,  who  is  also  the  contesting
respondent.
Learned  senior  counsel  appearing  for  the  first

--- Page 823 ---
respondent/contesting  respondent  submitted  that  as  of
today, there is no appeal filed as against the order dated
30.05.2026; that liberty may be reserved to the said
respondent to file an appeal (first appeal). 
Learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner
submitted that if such a liberty is reserved to the first
respondent herein, then the impugned order may be set
aside.
On hearing learned senior counsel for the respective
parties, we grant liberty to the first respondent herein to
file an appeal before the appellate authority so as to
assail order dated 30.05.2026 and also to seek interim
relief if such an appeal is filed before the appellate
authority. 
Further, we reserve liberty to the first respondent
herein to seek appropriate interim relief in MSA NO.19 of
2026.
In view of the above, the impugned order passed on IA
No.24 of 2026 dated 24.08.2026 is set aside.
The Special Leave Petition is disposed of in the
aforesaid terms.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

[Arising out of impugned final judgment and order dated 20-02-2025

P. ASHOK KUMAR                                     Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
THE GENERAL MANAGER OIL AND NATURAL GAS CORPORATION LTD. & ANR.
Respondent(s)
Date : 21-09-2026 This petition was called on for hearing today.
CORAM    HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MANOJ MISRA
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIJAY BISHNOI
For Petitioner(s)  Mr. Amit Pai, Adv.
                   Mr. S. Prabu Ramasubramanian, Adv.
                   Mr. Manoj Kumar A., Adv.
                   Mr. Ezhil Kumaran, Adv.
                   Mr. S.kavi Mukilan, Adv.
                   Mr. Ragul R, Adv.

For Respondent(s)  Mr. Sunil Kumar Jain, AOR
                   Mr. Naman Jain, Adv.
                   Ms. Reeta Chaudhary, Adv.
                   
                   
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. We have heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. The petitioner had applied for appointment as a
Junior  Fire  Supervisor.  One  of  the  eligibility
conditions was that an applicant, other than one
belonging to the specified category, should not be
1

--- Page 1007 ---
less  than  168  cm  in  height.  Admittedly,  the
petitioner  does  not  qualify  the  minimum  height
criteria,  yet  he  participated  in  the  selection
process without demur. After declaration of result,
the petitioner filed writ petition questioning the
height requirement on the ground that for men coming
from the State of Assam the minimum height required
is lower than what is for others. The High Court,
however, declined to interfere with the selection
process primarily on two counts:
(i)that the writ petitioner had participated in
the  selection  process  without  demur  despite
being fully aware that he would not be eligible
for selection; and
(ii) that at the time when the matter had come for
adjudication  several  years  had  passed  since
appointments  were  made,  therefore  any
interference would have adverse impact on public
interest. 
3. We do not find any error in the view taken by
the  High  Court.  The  Special  Leave  Petition  is,
accordingly, dismissed.
4. Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  stand
disposed of.        
(CHETAN ARORA)                             (AKSHAY KUMAR BHORIA)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS                        COURT MASTER (NSH)

present Special Leave Petition seeking grant of bail.
Accordingly,  the  Special  Leave  Petition  stands
dismissed.
 We,  however,  direct  the  Trial  Court  to
conclude the trial within a period of three months
from today.
It goes without sayin g that the prosecution as
well as the defence shall extend full cooperation for
expeditious conclusion of the trial.
We also make it clear that in the event trial
is not concluded within the aforesaid period for no
fault attributable to the petitioner, it would be
open for the petitioner to revive his prayer for
bail. 
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand
disposed of.
